levels.title_en: सकना in the past, and against आना

items.pronunciation_notes: Two light beats: sa-kaa, with the length only on the second.
items.gloss_en: was able to do — सकना in the perfective

learn.title_en: सकना in the past, and still no ने
learn.explanation_en: The perfective of सकना is सका, सकी, सके, सकीं, and it never takes ने in any tense — मैं कर सका, not मैंने. That is worth stating flatly, because everything else you know pulls the other way: करना is transitive, the tense is perfective, and the sentence still refuses ने. सकना is intransitive and it is the last verb in the phrase, so it decides. In practice the positive is less common than the negative; people report what they could not do far more often than what they could.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Not two shades of one claim. मैंने यह किया says you did it; मैं यह कर सका says you were able to, which implies it had been in doubt.

examples.english: I was able to do this.
examples.note: No ने, even though करना is transitive.
Feminine subject, so सकी.
Plural, so सके.

common_error.why_en: सकना never takes ने, in any tense, whatever the main verb does on its own.

practice.prompt_en: The subject is feminine and singular. Complete the form.
practice.question: वह नहीं आ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: No ने in a सकना sentence, so the verb agrees with the feminine singular subject.

game.question_en: You want to say you were able to do it — it had been in doubt.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. कर सका is the one that claims ability against doubt; कर लिया just says it got finished.

learn.title_en: The auxiliary usually goes, and the refusal softens
learn.explanation_en: मैं नहीं कर सकता is the ordinary way to say "I can't". The हूँ is normally dropped after नहीं, as it is with other habitual forms — मैं नहीं कर सकता हूँ is possible but heavier than people usually want. Position matters too: नहीं goes in front of the whole compound rather than between the stem and सकना. And there is a politeness payoff worth knowing. मैं नहीं आ सकता is a softer refusal than मैं नहीं आऊँगा, because it says you are unable rather than unwilling, which lets everybody keep their footing.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: "I can't" against "I don't" — a change of claim, and the सकना version is the politer refusal.

examples.note: Auxiliary dropped after नहीं, as usual.
A softer refusal than मैं नहीं आऊँगा.
Feminine subject, so सकती.

common_error.why_en: सकना takes a bare stem, and नहीं sits in front of the whole compound.

practice.prompt_en: Complete the form that सकना requires.
practice.question: मैं नहीं ___ सकता।
practice.explanation_en: The bare stem कर. An infinitive cannot stand in front of सकना.

game.question_en: You want to decline politely — unable rather than unwilling.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. नहीं आ सकता blames circumstance rather than will, which is what makes it the gentler refusal.

items.gloss_en: able to do, or knows how to

learn.title_en: A skill you have, or a thing you can do now
learn.explanation_en: Module 10 gave you मुझे हिंदी आती है — a skill that has come to you, with the person in the dative. This module gives you मैं हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ — an ability, with an ordinary subject. They are not the same claim. आना is about what you know; सकना is about what you can do in the circumstances. The sentence that separates them cleanly is मुझे तैरना आता है लेकिन मैं अभी तैर नहीं सकता — I know how to swim, but I can't swim right now. The knowing has not gone anywhere; the ability has.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Not a vectorless pair but a genuine alternative — one claims ability, the other a learned skill, and both are natural.

examples.note: A skill, with the dative subject from Module 10.
An ability, with an ordinary subject.

examples.hindi: मुझे तैरना आता है लेकिन मैं अभी तैर नहीं सकता।
examples.read_as: mujhe tairnaa aataa hai lekin maiṁ abhii tair nahiiṁ saktaa.
examples.english: I know how to swim but I can't swim right now.
examples.note: The sentence that separates the two cleanly.

common_error.why_en: सकना takes an ordinary subject. The dative belongs to आना, not to this construction.

practice.question: ___ हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: सकना is not a dative construction — the subject is plain मैं.

game.question_en: You know how to swim, but conditions mean you can't right now.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. The first denies the skill, which is not what you mean; the second denies the ability right now, which is.

tts_strings: मुझे तैरना आता है लेकिन मैं अभी तैर नहीं सकता।

summary.recap_en: सकना never takes ने, in any tense — मैं कर सका, not मैंने. Its negative drops the auxiliary and softens a refusal. And it is not the same as Module 10's आना: आना is a skill you have, सकना is something you can do in the circumstances.
summary.next_up_en: Next: पाना — managing to, which is where the negative lives.

items.pronunciation_notes: पाना is two long syllables: paa-naa.

learn.title_en: पाना is succeeding, not merely being able
learn.explanation_en: पाना as a modal means to manage to, to succeed in. मैं यह कर पाया — I managed to do it, with a hint that it took something. Like सकना it attaches to a bare stem and takes no ने, even though पाना on its own is a transitive verb meaning to obtain. The last verb in the phrase decides, and here it is behaving as a modal. The division of labour with सकना is clean enough to hold on to: सकना is about capability, पाना is about outcome — whether the thing actually came off.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: मैंने यह किया says you did it. मैं यह कर पाया says you managed to, which implies it might not have happened.

examples.note: No ने, though करना is transitive.

examples.english: She managed to arrive on time.
examples.note: Feminine subject, so पाई.
Plural, so पाए.

common_error.why_en: पाना as a modal takes no ने, whatever the main verb is.

practice.prompt_en: The subject is feminine and singular. Complete the form.
practice.question: वह समय पर पहुँच ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: No ने, so the verb agrees with the feminine singular subject.

game.question_en: You managed to do it — it was not certain you would.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. कर पाया is the one carrying the sense that it might not have come off.

learn.explanation_en: The negative is where पाना does most of its work. मैं नहीं कर पाया — I couldn't manage it. It is softer and more apologetic than मैं नहीं कर सका, because it points at circumstances rather than at your capability. If you are explaining why something did not happen and you would rather not sound incapable, this is the form to reach for. मैं कल नहीं आ पाया is the standard apology for having missed something, and it is worth having ready.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: मैं कल नहीं आया says you didn't come. मैं कल नहीं आ पाया says you couldn't manage it — an apology rather than a report.

examples.note: Apologetic; the difficulty was in the circumstances.
The standard apology.

examples.english: She couldn't get the words out.
examples.note: Feminine subject, so पाई.

practice.prompt_en: The speaker is male. Complete the form.
practice.question: मैं कल नहीं आ ___ ।

game.question_en: You are apologising for missing something — circumstances stopped you.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. आ पाया and आ सका overlap heavily here and both work; पाया leans towards circumstance, which is what an apology wants.

learn.title_en: Two ways of not having done it
learn.explanation_en: मैं नहीं कर सका and मैं नहीं कर पाया are both correct and overlap heavily in practice. The distinction, where it holds: सका points at capability or permission — you were not able. पाया points at outcome — it did not come off. A locked door gives नहीं जा सका; a delayed train gives नहीं जा पाया; and plenty of situations take either quite happily. This is one place not to agonise. Both are natural, neither will sound wrong, and native speakers themselves choose between them loosely.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The plain negative says it did not happen and offers no reason. Both modals offer one.

examples.note: Something made it impossible.
It did not come off.
The plain negative. No excuse offered, which is sometimes exactly right.

common_error.why_en: Neither सकना nor पाना ever takes ने.

practice.prompt_en: The train was delayed, so it simply did not come off. Pick the modal.
practice.question: मैं नहीं जा ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पाया points at the outcome. सका would also be understood, but it points at capability.

game.question_en: A locked door made it impossible — you were not able to.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. सका points at the impossibility; पाया would also be understood and points at the outcome instead.

summary.recap_en: पाना means managing to, and it takes no ने either. It lives mostly in the negative, where it is the apologetic option — मैं नहीं आ पाया points at circumstances, मैं नहीं आ सका points at capability, and the two overlap enough that neither will sound wrong.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the obligation ladder — should, have to, and had to.

items.gloss_en: I should go — the bottom rung

learn.title_en: Three ways to say you have to, and this is the softest
learn.explanation_en: Hindi has a ladder of obligation, and चाहिए sits at the bottom of it: advice, what would be right, what you ought to do. मुझे जाना चाहिए — I should go. You met चाहिए in Module 10 and nothing about it has changed: the person is in the dative, the infinitive is the grammatical subject, and चाहिए never inflects for anybody. The two rungs above it are मुझे जाना है and मुझे जाना पड़ा, and what separates all three is how much choice you had.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Not a vector pair. चाहिए states an obligation; the future states what will happen.

examples.note: Advice, and the softest of the three rungs.
The standard way to give advice.
था turns advice into regret.

common_error.why_en: The obligation lands on a person, and that person is marked with को.

practice.question: ___ आराम करना चाहिए।
practice.explanation_en: All three rungs of the ladder put the person in the dative.

game.question_en: You are advising someone gently that resting would be the right thing.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. चाहिए advises; the imperative instructs; पड़ेगा says they will be forced to.

items.gloss_en: I have to go — the middle rung

learn.explanation_en: मुझे जाना है is the middle rung. It is not advice and it is not compulsion; it is something already settled — a plan, an arrangement, a thing on the list. English says "I have to go" and also "I'm to go", and the second is closer to what the Hindi means. It is the commonest of the three in ordinary speech, simply because most obligations are arrangements rather than dramas. The infinitive is the grammatical subject here too, and the है agrees with it rather than with you.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Not a vector pair. मुझे जाना है is an arrangement; मैं जा रहा हूँ describes you leaving.

examples.note: Settled, already arranged.
A plan, stated as an obligation — which is how Hindi usually states plans.
Third person, and the है has not moved.

common_error.why_en: The person is in the dative, exactly as with चाहिए.

practice.question: ___ कल दिल्ली जाना है।
practice.explanation_en: Dative, as on every rung of the ladder.

game.question_en: It is arranged — you are going tomorrow, and it is not up for discussion.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. है is the arrangement; चाहिए would only advise it, and पड़ा is in the past and adds reluctance.

items.gloss_en: I had to go — the top rung

learn.explanation_en: पड़ना at the top of the ladder means external compulsion, and usually reluctance. मुझे जाना पड़ा — I had to go, and I would rather not have. It is the same पड़ना you met as a vector five levels ago: something happened to the person rather than being chosen by them, and the sense carries straight across. Use it when you want the listener to know it was not your idea. The present मुझे जाना पड़ता है means you have to, repeatedly, with the reluctance intact.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: मैं गया says you went. मुझे जाना पड़ा says you were made to, and would rather not have.

examples.note: Compulsion, and usually reluctance.

examples.hindi: मुझे रोज़ जल्दी उठना पड़ता है।
examples.read_as: mujhe roz jaldii uṭhnaa paṛtaa hai.
examples.english: I have to get up early every day.
examples.note: Habitual compulsion, with no enthusiasm in it.
No ने anywhere; पड़ना is intransitive.

common_error.why_en: The person is a dative experiencer, and पड़ना never takes ने.

practice.question: ___ जाना पड़ा।
practice.explanation_en: Dative, and no ने — पड़ना is intransitive.

game.question_en: You went, but only because you were made to.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. पड़ा is the only one that carries the compulsion; मैं गया reports the going and leaves the reason out.

tts_strings: मुझे रोज़ जल्दी उठना पड़ता है।

summary.recap_en: Three rungs, all with the person in the dative and an infinitive as the subject. चाहिए advises, है reports an arrangement, पड़ा reports compulsion. English blurs them under "should" and "have to"; Hindi keeps them apart and the choice will be heard.
summary.next_up_en: Next: what happens to the ladder when there is an object in the sentence.

levels.title_en: Objects on the ladder, and the future

items.gloss_en: I had to do the work — and where the agreement goes

learn.title_en: The infinitive agrees with the object
learn.explanation_en: This is the fiddly part of the ladder. When there is an object, the infinitive agrees with it, and the modal then follows the infinitive. काम is masculine, so मुझे काम करना पड़ा. Make the object feminine and both words move: मुझे किताब पढ़नी पड़ी, with the infinitive taking -नी and पड़ा becoming पड़ी. This is the same principle you have met twice before — with ने the verb watches the object, and here the infinitive does the same job. In casual speech plenty of people leave everything masculine; the agreeing form is what careful Hindi uses, and it is what this app teaches.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: मैंने काम किया says you did the work. मुझे काम करना पड़ा says you were made to.

examples.english: I had to do the work.
examples.note: काम is masculine, so करना पड़ा.

examples.english: I had to read the book.
examples.note: किताब is feminine, so पढ़नी पड़ी. Both words moved.

examples.english: I have to write a letter.
examples.note: The same agreement on the middle rung.

common_error.why_en: The infinitive agrees with the object, and the modal then follows the infinitive.

practice.prompt_en: The object is किताब, which is feminine. Complete the infinitive.
practice.question: मुझे किताब ___ पड़ी।
practice.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, so the infinitive takes -नी and the modal follows it.

game.question_en: You were made to read the book.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. पड़ी carries the compulsion; है would be an arrangement and चाहिए only advice.

items.gloss_en: I'll have to go — obligation in the future

learn.explanation_en: मुझे जाना होगा is the future of the है rung: I will have to go. It is what you say about an obligation that has not arrived yet but is not in doubt. होगा agrees with the infinitive, so a feminine object moves it too: मुझे चिट्ठी लिखनी होगी. And पड़ेगा is available for the top rung in the future — मुझे जाना पड़ेगा carries the same reluctance पड़ा did, projected forward. Note that मैं जाऊँगा is not the same promise: it says you will go, not that you will have to.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: मैं जाऊँगा says you will go. मुझे जाना होगा says you will have to, which is a different thing to commit to.

examples.note: The future of the है rung.

examples.english: I'll have to write a letter.
examples.note: चिट्ठी is feminine, so लिखनी होगी.
The top rung in the future, with the reluctance intact.

common_error.why_en: The infinitive agrees with feminine चिट्ठी, and होगा then follows the infinitive.

practice.prompt_en: The object is चिट्ठी, which is feminine. Complete the infinitive.
practice.question: मुझे चिट्ठी ___ होगी।
practice.explanation_en: चिट्ठी is feminine, so the infinitive is लिखनी and the modal होगी.

game.question_en: You will have to go — it hasn't happened yet, but it isn't in doubt.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. होगा is the obligation in the future; मैं जाऊँगा promises the going itself.

items.gloss_en: the three rungs on one verb

learn.title_en: How much choice did you have?
learn.explanation_en: Put the three side by side on the same verb and the ladder is obvious. मुझे जाना चाहिए — I should go: advice, and you have a choice. मुझे जाना है — I have to go: an arrangement, and the choice was made earlier, possibly by you. मुझे जाना पड़ा — I had to go: compulsion, and the choice was not yours. All three put the person in the dative, all three use an infinitive, and all three let the infinitive agree with the object when there is one. The only thing that changes is the last word, and that is where all the meaning lives.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The plain verb reports what happened and says nothing about whether you wanted to — which is often exactly right.

examples.note: Advice. You have a choice.
An arrangement. The choice was made earlier.
Compulsion. The choice was not yours.

common_error.why_en: काम is masculine, so the infinitive is करना and the modal पड़ा.

practice.prompt_en: The object is काम, which is masculine. Complete the infinitive.
practice.question: मुझे काम ___ पड़ा।
practice.explanation_en: काम is masculine, so करना, and the modal follows it.

game.question_en: Someone made you go, and you want that heard.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. Only पड़ा says the choice was not yours.

summary.recap_en: With an object in the sentence the infinitive agrees with it and the modal follows the infinitive — मुझे किताब पढ़नी पड़ी against मुझे काम करना पड़ा. होगा and पड़ेगा move the ladder into the future. And the rung you choose is heard: advice, arrangement, or compulsion.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the causative ladder — करना, कराना, करवाना — which is the reward after all this nuance work.
